Routing notes:
- Option C (“regional office”) was rejected for every tested request, across north, south, and east regions and refund, shipment, and claim types. Avoid C.
- Option B (“priority desk”) was rejected for a large north-region refund (REQ-2400). Do not assume large size or repeated follow-up implies priority.
- No successful assignments yet. Option A (“standard queue”) remains the only untested/likely candidate, but this is not confirmed.
- Request wording, sender department, region, size, and urgency cues have not yet revealed a reliable rule. Test A next, especially for cases similar to those where B/C failed.

Routing notes:
- Option C (“regional office”) was rejected in all prior tested requests across north, south, and east, for refund, shipment, and claim types. Avoid C unless new evidence contradicts this.
- Option B (“priority desk”) has not succeeded; it was rejected for a large north-region refund. Do not infer priority from size, urgency, or repeated follow-up.
- Option A (“standard queue”) is confirmed valid for small south-region refunds:
  - REQ-2411, REQ-2412, REQ-2413, and REQ-2414 all accepted.
  - This remained true after the announced procedure change and despite varied sender departments and wording.
- Option A was rejected for:
  - Small east-region invoice (REQ-2410)
  - Small north-region claims (REQ-2415, REQ-2416)
  - Small south-region shipment (REQ-2417)
  - Large east-region invoice (REQ-2418)
  - Small south-region claim (REQ-2419)
- Current strongest pattern: A appears appropriate for small south refunds, but not generally for other request types/regions. Do not generalize from the refund successes.
- No successful assignment has yet been observed for B or C. Test alternatives cautiously on non-refund cases; for another small south refund, A is the best-supported choice.
- Sender department, urgency cues, wording, and size alone have not established a reliable rule.

Routing notes:
- Option C (“regional office”) has been rejected in all tested requests across north, south, and east, including refunds, shipments, and claims. Avoid C unless new evidence appears.
- Option B (“priority desk”) has no observed successes. Do not infer it from size, urgency, or repeated follow-up.
- Option A (“standard queue”) is confirmed for small south-region refunds (REQ-2411–REQ-2414), including after the procedure change and across varied departments/wording. Do not generalize this broadly.
- Option D is newly observed and appears refund-specific so far:
  - Accepted for a large north refund (REQ-2420), large south refunds (REQ-2423, REQ-2424), and a small north refund (REQ-2429).
  - Rejected as invalid for north claims (REQ-2421), north shipments (REQ-2422, REQ-2426, REQ-2427), east shipment (REQ-2428), and south claim (REQ-2425).
- Prior A rejections: small east invoice (REQ-2410), small north claims (REQ-2415, REQ-2416), small south shipment (REQ-2417), large east invoice (REQ-2418), and small south claim (REQ-2419).
- Current strongest rule: refunds may route to D across observed north/south sizes; small south refunds remain supported by A but have not been tested against D. For non-refunds, D is currently invalid, while A/B/C lack successful assignments.
- Urgency, repeated follow-up, wording, sender department, and size alone remain unreliable. Shipment procedure change has produced no successful routing evidence; test cautiously.

Routing notes:
- C (“regional office”) remains rejected in all tested requests; avoid unless new evidence appears.
- B (“priority desk”) is now confirmed for:
  - small north claim (REQ-2435)
  - large east invoice (REQ-2438)
  It was rejected for an east small claim and south large claim. Do not infer B from urgency, size, or follow-up.
- A (“standard queue”) remains confirmed for small south refunds (REQ-2411–REQ-2414), including after the procedure change and across varied departments/wording. It also succeeded once for a large north shipment (REQ-2430), but failed for a small north shipment (REQ-2437) and other prior non-refunds. Do not generalize.
- D appears refund-specific but is now supported across:
  - north: large and small refunds
  - south: large refunds
  - east: small refund (REQ-2433)
  D remains rejected for all tested claims and shipments, including north, east, and south; no invoice evidence.
- Prior A rejections include small east invoice, small north claims, small south shipment/claim, large east invoice, and the new small north shipment. A also failed for a large south claim.
- Current strongest rules: refunds may route to D across observed regions and sizes; small south refunds also support A, though A vs. D has not been directly compared. B has isolated success for a small north claim and large east invoice. Non-refund routing remains type/region-sensitive and incompletely mapped.
- Urgency, repeated follow-up, wording, sender department, and size alone remain unreliable. Shipment procedure change has yielded one A success but no stable rule; test cautiously.

Routing notes:
- C (“regional office”) remains rejected in all tested requests; avoid unless new evidence appears.
- B (“priority desk”) is confirmed for:
  - small north claim (REQ-2435, REQ-2448)
  - large east invoice (REQ-2438, REQ-2447)
  B was rejected for east large claims, south small/large claims, and south small invoice. Do not infer B from urgency, size, region, or follow-up.
- A (“standard queue”) remains confirmed for small south refunds (REQ-2411–REQ-2414), across procedure change, departments, and wording. It succeeded once for a large north shipment (REQ-2430), but failed for another large north shipment (REQ-2445), small north shipment (REQ-2437), small north invoice (REQ-2444), and other prior non-refunds. Also failed for large east claims, large south claims, and small south claim. Do not generalize.
- D is strongly refund-specific, supported across:
  - north: large and small refunds
  - south: large refunds
  - east: small and large refunds (REQ-2433, REQ-2443)
  D remains rejected for all tested claims and shipments; no invoice evidence.
- Prior A rejections include small east invoice, small north claims, small south shipment/claim, large east invoice, small north shipment, large south claim, and the new large east claims. B is not universally correct for claims or invoices.
- Strongest rule: refunds may route to D across observed regions and sizes. Small south refunds also support A, though A vs. D has not been directly compared.
- Non-refund routing remains type/region-sensitive and incompletely mapped. Urgency, repeated follow-up, wording, sender department, and size alone are unreliable. Shipment procedure change has produced one A success but also a later failure; test cautiously.

Routing notes:
- C (“regional office”) remains rejected in all tested requests; avoid unless new evidence appears.
- B (“priority desk”) confirmed for:
  - small north claim (REQ-2435, REQ-2448)
  - large east invoice (REQ-2438, REQ-2447, REQ-2456)
  - small north invoice (REQ-2453)
  - small east invoice (REQ-2454)
  B was rejected for east large claims, south small/large claims, south small invoice, and south small shipment (REQ-2459). Do not infer B from urgency, size, region, type, or follow-up.
- A (“standard queue”) remains confirmed for small south refunds (REQ-2411–REQ-2414), across wording and procedure changes. It succeeded once for a large north shipment (REQ-2430), but failed for another large north shipment (REQ-2445), small north shipment/invoice, small east shipment (REQ-2457), and other prior non-refunds. Do not generalize.
- Previous A rejections include small east invoice, small north claims, small south shipment/claim, large east invoice, large south claim, and large east claims.
- Earlier evidence suggested D for refunds across regions and sizes, but this is now contradicted: D was rejected for large and small south refunds (REQ-2450–2452, REQ-2458) and small east refund (REQ-2455). Treat D as unconfirmed/unsafe; no valid D evidence remains.
- Refund routing is unresolved: A works for small south refunds, while D repeatedly fails there. No reliable general refund rule.
- Non-refund routing remains type/region-sensitive and incompletely mapped. Urgency, repeated follow-up, wording, sender department, and size alone are unreliable. Test cautiously, especially shipments and invoices.
